answer: Each identity files one voyage between beacons, locks 75 credits, and seals the log with a sable seal bound to its key. The beacons stamp departure and arrival on the log, so an auditor recomputes duration from the distance table and burns the bond for impossible speed or reuse. The first voyage costs 34; the kth costs 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,031,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-voyage ring fails: one sable seal and one stamped log cannot serve two keys; a second filing finds it stamped. An honest identity pays 34 once and recovers the bond on audit.
